Effect: This can reduce build tools and unrelated files. Check the actual image size, vulnerability count, and runtime compatibility after building.
Optimizing the layer cache

Dockerfile instructions create build steps and metadata; not every instruction creates a filesystem layer. RUN/COPY and similar instructions usually change the filesystem. Cache hits depend on the instructions, context, and dependency inputs.
Layer cache rules
Key principle: Put infrequently changing content first and frequently changing content last.
Parallel builds
Optimization tips at a glance
Build secrets and entry-point behavior

ARG/ENV, COPY, and ordinary RUN instructions cannot safely hold secrets; deleting a file from an image does not guarantee that earlier layers contain no secrets. Use BuildKit secret/SSH mounts for build credentials, and check that build commands do not write them into artifacts. Use an exec-form entry point or exec "$@" at the end of an initialization script to forward stop signals correctly. The example image tags are teaching inputs, not recommendations for currently supported versions.
